system_description.narrative_summary: The dominant narrative is that the late-September 2026 Trump–Xi meetings produced high pageantry and symbolic concessions but failed to resolve core strategic tensions between the United States and China. As an open system, the summit functioned as a node linking political signaling, negotiated trade tweaks (tariff trims, a ~$60bn low-tariff regime), an AI dialogue channel, and security rhetoric around Taiwan; information, political legitimacy, capital flows, and market expectations passed through the summit and generated feedbacks that reshape domestic politics, allied trust, and commercial strategy. The encounter reduced some transactional frictions while leaving fundamental competition in technology, supply chains, and regional security unresolved, creating downstream adaptations across firms, governments, and markets.
system_description.scope: Inside the system: the bilateral state visit and follow-on meetings; negotiated trade measures (tariff reductions/low-tariff regime); establishment of an AI dialogue; public diplomacy and media spectacle; security-related rhetoric and informal assurances around Taiwan and Iran; corporate and investor responses (batteries, automakers, investment deals); allied and partner reactions; short-term market and sentiment shifts.
system_description.super_system: The global geopolitical-economic order — great-power competition and multilateral trade/technology governance.
adjacent_subsystems: US domestic politics and electoral signaling
Global technology and critical-minerals supply chains
International trade and allied economic policy (EU, Japan, ASEAN)

variables.name: Diplomatic signaling intensity
variables.description: The continuous intensity and visibility of public diplomatic gestures, pageantry and official signaling between negotiating actors.

variables.name: Trade barrier level
variables.description: The average effective height of tariff and non-tariff barriers constraining cross-border goods and services flows.

variables.name: Low-tariff agreement scope
variables.description: The breadth and share of goods and services covered by preferential or reduced-tariff arrangements between parties.

variables.name: AI cooperation depth
variables.description: The substantive depth and institutionalization of cooperative channels, information exchange and joint measures in artificial intelligence.

variables.name: Security tension level
variables.description: The prevailing intensity of strategic-security frictions and perceived military risk across contested regional issues.

variables.name: Technological competition intensity
variables.description: The degree of competitive pressure in key technology domains, including R&D rivalry, export controls and strategic decoupling incentives.

variables.name: Supply-chain fragmentation
variables.description: The extent to which production networks are geographically dispersed, re-shored or segmented across alternative supplier blocs.

variables.name: Investor sentiment
variables.description: The aggregate market perception and risk appetite of investors toward assets exposed to bilateral political and economic dynamics.

variables.name: Capital flow rate
variables.description: The volume per unit time of cross-border financial inflows and outflows into assets and sectors linked to the bilateral relationship.

variables.name: Market volatility
variables.description: The realized short- to medium-term variability of asset prices and exchange rates influenced by geopolitical-economic shocks.

variables.name: Corporate restructuring rate
variables.description: The rate at which firms alter investment, supply-chain design, joint ventures and market strategies in response to strategic pressures.

variables.name: Allied trust level
variables.description: The aggregate level of confidence and policy alignment among third-party partners and alliances regarding bilateral commitments.

variables.name: Domestic political legitimacy
variables.description: The perceived domestic approval and institutional legitimacy of national leadership as influenced by foreign-policy engagements.

variables.name: Regulatory uncertainty
variables.description: The prevailing unpredictability and clarity of policy and regulatory rules affecting trade, investment and strategic technologies.

variables.name: Media spectacle intensity
variables.description: The magnitude and salience of public media coverage and symbolic framing of events and interactions.

variables.name: Policy coordination capacity
variables.description: The institutional ability and bandwidth to design, negotiate and implement sustained cross-jurisdictional policy measures.

catalysts.title: Two scheduled follow-up Trump–Xi meetings
catalysts.description: Two additional bilateral meetings the leaders agreed to hold, likely focused on trade and strategic issues; high-visibility opportunities for signaling.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Trump and Xi to meet twice more after summit fails to resolve tensions' (2026-09-27/29).

catalysts.title: Release of trade-talk details
catalysts.description: Publication of negotiating details and product lists for the tariff/trade concessions that the U.S. and China agreed to discuss.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Details on US, China trade talks to come on Monday, says Greer' (2026-09-27).

catalysts.title: $60bn low-tariff regime implementation
catalysts.description: Operational rollout and tariff reductions on the agreed $60 billion of goods, including administrative lists and phased tariff cuts.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'US and China agree $60bn low tariff regime' / 'China, US agree tariff cuts on $60 billion of goods' (2026-09-28/29).

catalysts.title: Institutionalization of US–China AI dialogue
catalysts.description: Negotiation and establishment of formal channels, working groups and information exchanges on AI cooperation and risk-management.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'U.S., China Agree to Trim Tariffs, Start AI Dialogue' and 'China, US agree to AI dialogue' (2026-09-27/28).

catalysts.title: U.S. actions on critical-minerals supply chains
catalysts.description: U.S. measures aiming to curb China's dominance in critical minerals (export controls, subsidy shifts, sourcing initiatives) that alter supply networks.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'See How the U.S. Is Attacking China’s Control of Critical Minerals' (2026-09-27).

catalysts.title: China's agricultural tariff-list clarifications/exclusions
catalysts.description: Refinements to China's announced tariff cuts for U.S. farm goods—negotiations and public clarifications, including exclusions like soybeans.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'China to cut tariffs on US farm goods, but list excludes soybeans' and tariff coverage reporting (2026-09-28).

catalysts.title: Near-term investor and market volatility reaction
catalysts.description: Short-term capital flows and volatility responding to perceptions that the summit delivered spectacle but limited substantive breakthroughs.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Chinese Equities Extend Losses'; 'GM warns on US market'; 'spectacle over substance' summaries (2026-09-27 to 29).
